figures.finding: A child of seven to twelve may do light work in culture, art, sports or advertising (from thirteen, light work generally; fifteen for ordinary work); no permit is applied for, but the employer enters the child in the employment register ahead of the start (five working days, as the Labour Inspectorate's page says now; the 2024 translation said ten) with the legal representative's consent, the duties and the school obligation, and the inspector, who checks the child wants to work, may refuse, consent being presumed when the term passes. Hours: seven to twelve, 2 a day and 12 a week in term outside school hours, 3 and 15 in holidays; a schoolchild in culture or art may work 3 hours a day and 12 a week in term. Under seven, no work. The rule is the Act's for any employment in culture and art, so it reaches a young writer or director as well.

value.permit: entry in the employment register; labour inspector may refuse (consent presumed)

figures.applies: Nationwide; night-work limits for minors weren't found in the translation read.

sources.said: Minors of 7–12 years of age are allowed to do light work in the field of culture, art, sports or advertising. … 1) in the case of an employee who is 7–12 years of age – 2 hours a day and 12 hours over a period of seven days during a quarter of an academic year outside of school hours and 3 hours a day and 15 hours over a period of seven days during school holidays;

(4 2 ) If a minor who is subject to the obligation to attend school performs light work in the field of culture, art, sports or advertising, their working time during a quarter of an academic year outside of school hours may be 3 hours a day and 12 hours over a period of seven days. … (6) The labour inspector’s consent for allowing a minor of 7–12 years of age to work is presumed if the term provided in subsection 3 of this section has passed and the labour inspector has not refused to grant consent.

Employers are not required to apply for the Labour Inspectorate’s permission for employing a young person under 13 years of age; however, they must add a respective entry in the employment register five working days before the 7–12-year-old starts working . … Children under the age of 7 are prohibited from working pursuant to the Employment Contracts Act.

figures.finding: A minor's own agreement to an employment contract without a legal representative's prior consent is void unless the representative approves it afterwards; the representative's consent is needed for every employee under eighteen, and for a seven-to-twelve-year-old it is filed with the Labour Inspectorate. No set-aside of earnings was found. The rule reaches any employment, writing or directing included.

value.binding: legal representative's prior consent (or later approval); for 7-12, consent filed with the Labour Inspectorate

figures.applies: Nationwide; commissions outside employment (authors' contracts) fall under the General Part of the Civil Code Act, not reached.

sources.said: (1) An expression of will made by a minor for entry into an employment contract without the prior consent of a legal representative is void, unless the legal representative subsequently approves the expression of will.
When concluding an employment contract with an employee who is a minor (i.e., an employee under the age of 18), the employer shall ask for the consent of his or her legal representative.

figures.finding: The Estonian Film Institute's support may be sought only by a private legal person registered in Estonia or a sole proprietor entered in the commercial register, never by a natural person as such, so a young writer, director or producer applies through a company or as a registered sole proprietor.

value.applicant: Estonian-registered private legal person or sole proprietor in the commercial register

figures.applies: Minister of Culture regulation no. 25 of 31 December 2018 as amended, as its explanatory memorandum states § 4.

sources.said: Paragrahviga 4 kehtestatakse nõuded taotlejale. Lõikes 1 kehtestatakse subjektide ring, kellele toetus on suunatud ning mille kohaselt saab taotlejaks olla Eestis registreeritud eraõiguslik juriidiline isik ja äriregistrisse kantud füüsilisest isikust ettevõtja. Seega ei saa toetusi taotleda avalik-õiguslikud juriidilised isikud ning füüsilised isikud.

figures.finding: The Estonian Actors' Union sets no age: full members are those working as professional actors or in a near creative field, and young members are students of acting or a near field (not voting); members delegate the exercise of their performers' property rights to the Union.

value.full: professional actors or near creative field
value.young: students in acting or near field, no vote

figures.applies: The Union's statutes as published; writers' and directors' unions not read.
